method: A need runs only when a typed query (or a short set of them, one per named record) in the grammar of typed_query_grammar.md, checked against typed_check.rs/typed_match.rs, returns rows whose own attributes state the answer over records this recipe's build makes, each attribute traced to its writer (a claim field the reader reads, a `by` or protocol fold, a metadata source, or RESOLVE) in corpus-engine/src/enrichment and the `sovereign recipe validate` output (all twelve exit 0); a need whose weakest required part is declared but not written onto any record or not reachable by the query is inert, and one whose required part is not declared at all (or only in guidance prose) is inexpressible. Edge cases the owner's words do not name were not used to fail a need, and per-record argmax with a date bound was accepted as answering a per-record state question.

use_cases.record_types_note: organization and correspondent are metadata-sourced from from/to/cc; candidate, opening and application are RESOLVE-decided with statement kinds about them. Every type the seven needs require gets records.

needs.need: For each opening, which candidates are in play and at what stage (applied, screen, onsite, offer, hired, rejected, withdrew)?
needs.declared_by: application.opening (ref, by=agree), application.candidate (ref, by=agree), application.stage derived = fold application_stage (protocol over stage_move/offer_terms/offer_response)
needs.executed_by: validator: `derived: application.stage <- fold application_stage by protocol, after RESOLVE`; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived.rs:148 (derived value written on the record), resolution_derived/protocol.rs:31 (protocol fold over the record's claims); document_date stamped from change.document.date
needs.why: One query per opening lists its applications, each row carrying stage and the candidate it links.

needs.need: Who referred or sourced each candidate (an employee, an agency, or the candidate applied directly)?
needs.declared_by: application.channel (closed text, by=earliest), application.referrer (ref correspondent, by=earliest), application.agency (ref organization, by=earliest)
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/read_fields.rs:51 (a `by` subject field folds onto the record), read_fields.rs:370; earliest orders by the document clock, which change.document.date supplies (resolution_derived.rs:283-300)
needs.why: The earliest-introduction fold lands channel, referrer and agency on the application; refs resolve to the header-sourced correspondent and organization records.

needs.need: Who interviewed a candidate, for which opening, on what date, and what each interviewer recommended?
needs.declared_by: interview_feedback (claim, subject application): interviewer (ref correspondent), interview_date (time), round, recommendation (closed)
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/statement_refs.rs:137-142 (a statement's ref holds the record its reading names)
needs.why: Each feedback claim carries its interviewer, date and recommendation and reaches the application, hence candidate and opening.

needs.need: What we offered (base salary, currency, start date) and whether the offer was accepted, declined or revised.
needs.declared_by: offer_terms (claim, subject application): base_salary, currency, start_date, move; application.offer_status derived = fold offer_status (protocol)
needs.executed_by: validator: `derived: application.offer_status <- fold offer_status by protocol`; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived.rs:148 (derived value written on the record), resolution_derived/protocol.rs:31 (protocol fold over the record's claims)
needs.why: Offer claims carry the terms; the protocol fold puts extended/revised/accepted/declined on the application.

needs.need: When a candidate moved stage, and on whose say-so.
needs.declared_by: stage_move (claim, subject application): move, decider_role, decided_by (ref correspondent), effective_on; document_date stamp
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86; validator: `document fields: document_date <- date ... stamped on each claim`
needs.why: Each move is a cited claim with its date stamp, effective_on and the decider.

needs.need: Which agencies are owed a fee for a hire, and how much.
needs.declared_by: agency_fee (claim, subject application): amount, currency, fee_percent; fee_terms (claim, subject organization): fee_percent, flat_fee
needs.why: Hires by agency and any fee an agency's own invoice states are held, but the fee owed before an invoice is fee_percent x the offer's base_salary, which no fold or query computes; it is not declared anywhere.

needs.need: A candidate who applies to two openings is one person with two applications.
needs.declared_by: candidate identity = [email] + identity_criterion; application identity_criterion (one candidate for one opening)
needs.executed_by: validator: `identity: candidate -> RESOLVE under its identity_criterion`; validator: `identity: application -> RESOLVE under its identity_criterion`
needs.why: RESOLVE makes one candidate record and one application per opening, linked by application.candidate.

use_cases.record_types_note: organization and contract are RESOLVE-decided and get records. The contract owner is `ref of person`; `person` is an undeclared base kind that no statement is about and no source supplies, so the document reader makes no record of it and the owner reference holds nothing.

needs.need: Every contract with its counterparty, type (master agreement, statement of work, NDA, lease), and owner on our side.
needs.declared_by: contract.counterparty (ref organization, by=agree), contract.contract_type (closed, by=agree), contract.owner (ref person, by=most)
needs.why: Counterparty and type run, but owner points at the base kind `person`, of which no record exists, so every owner reading is unresolved and dropped (read_fields.rs:93-115, statement_refs.rs:137-142); validate gives no warning because `person` is not a declared type (document_read/schema.rs:186-216).

needs.need: Each contract's effective date, end date, and notice period for renewal or termination.
needs.declared_by: term_dates (claim, subject contract): as_of, effective, ends; renewal_term: as_of, renewal_notice, termination_notice
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86; argmax over a time attribute: typed.rs:469-533
needs.why: Per contract, the term statement with the latest as_of gives the current effective and end dates and notice periods, amendments included.

needs.need: The contract's value and currency, and how an amendment changed it.
needs.declared_by: price_term (claim, subject contract): as_of, instrument, value, currency, basis
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86
needs.why: Every price statement is held with its as_of and the instrument that set it, so the original and each amended value list side by side.

needs.need: Which amendments apply to which contract, in order, and what each changed.
needs.declared_by: amendment (claim, subject contract): amendment_no, signed_on, effective, changes (closed), summary
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86
needs.why: Each amendment claim reaches its contract and carries its number, effective date and what it changed.

needs.need: Which contracts are in force today, and which were in force on a given past date.
needs.declared_by: change.supersedes = { term_dates = as_of, renewal_term = as_of, price_term = as_of }; notice (claim)
needs.why: change.supersedes is read only by the tension comparability pass (analysis/tension_fields.rs:93-102), so a superseded term still matches a date filter, and an auto-renewed term past its written end date has no statement covering the date; selecting the set of contracts whose current term covers a date needs each contract's state at that date.

needs.need: Which contracts renew automatically and the date by which notice must be given.
needs.declared_by: renewal_term.auto_renews (closed), renewal_term.notice_deadline (time, only where the document states it)
needs.why: Auto-renewal runs, but the notice date is usually end date minus the notice period, and nothing derives a date by arithmetic (FoldBy is first/agree/most/all/earliest/latest/protocol, shared/crates/understanding-vocab/src/ontology/derived.rs:143-158).

needs.need: A statement of work belongs to its master agreement.
needs.declared_by: contract.master (ref contract, by=agree)
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/read_fields.rs:51 (a `by` subject field folds onto the record), read_fields.rs:370; contract is a RESOLVE-decided type, so a master named in the document is a particular the reference lands on (document_read/window.rs:63-92)
needs.why: The master reference folds onto the SOW record and links two contract records.

needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/read_fields.rs:51 (a `by` subject field folds onto the record), read_fields.rs:370

needs.need: Which version of each policy is in force now, and which was in force on a given past date.

needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86; argmax over a time attribute with an lt bound: typed.rs:469-533, typed_match.rs:309-345
needs.why: Per policy, the decision with the latest effective date before the asked date names the version (or the retirement) in force then; change.supersedes itself executes only in the tension pass, and a decision with no stated effective date is set aside and counted in the answer's notes.

needs.need: When and by whom each policy was approved, amended or retired.
needs.declared_by: policy_decision: action, decided_by (text), decided_on, effective, minute_ref
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86

needs.need: What each amendment changed (the clause before and after).
needs.declared_by: clause_change (claim, subject clause): change, before, after, effective; clause.policy (ref policy, no `by`)
needs.why: Before/after wording runs per clause, but the clause's policy is declared without `by`, so it stays on each statement and never reaches the clause record (read_fields.rs:41-54 folds only attributes with `by`); no query links an amendment's clause changes to the policy amended, and validate is silent.

needs.need: Which policy replaced a retired one.
needs.declared_by: policy_decision.replaced_by (ref policy)
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/statement_refs.rs:137-142 (a statement's ref holds the record its reading names)
needs.why: The retirement claim's replaced_by lands on the replacing policy record.

needs.need: Every rule a policy imposes (who must or must not do what) with the clause it comes from.
needs.declared_by: rule (directive claim, deontic require/forbid/permit, subject clause): bearer, conditions, exceptions
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86
needs.why: Each rule is a directive claim about its clause.

needs.declared_by: purchase_request (claim): requester (ref contact), item, quantity, quantity_unit, estimated_cost, currency

needs.why: Each request claim carries every asked field; the requester lands on the header-sourced contact.

needs.need: Who approved or rejected each request, and when; requests above 10,000 need two approvals.

needs.need: The purchase order a request became, its supplier and its total.
needs.declared_by: purchase_order (claim, subject purchase): reference, supplier (ref supplier), order_total, currency
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/statement_refs.rs:137-142 (a statement's ref holds the record its reading names)

needs.need: The invoices against each purchase order and whether the invoiced amount matches the order.
needs.declared_by: invoice (claim, subject purchase): invoiced_amount; tension `mismatch` between purchase_order and invoice
needs.why: Invoices per purchase list, but the match is declared only as a tension, whose edges are no relation the typed query reaches (typed_check.rs:278-330 admits declared relation types and refs only), and no filter compares an invoice's amount with its order's total (typed_check.rs:216-275 compares an attribute to a literal).

needs.need: Each order's status (requested, approved, ordered, delivered, invoiced, paid, cancelled).
needs.declared_by: purchase.status derived = fold purchase_status (protocol)
needs.executed_by: validator: `derived: purchase.status <- fold purchase_status by protocol`; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived.rs:148 (derived value written on the record), resolution_derived/protocol.rs:31 (protocol fold over the record's claims)
needs.why: The protocol fold over dated claims puts the status on the purchase.

needs.need: Our suppliers, with their contacts, and how much we have ordered from each this year.
needs.declared_by: supplier (metadata), contact.organization (ref supplier), purchase_order.order_total
needs.why: Suppliers and contacts run, but the amount ordered per supplier is a sum of order totals and the query aggregates only none/count/argmax/argmin (typed.rs:134-145).

use_cases.record_types_note: incident (event), service and action_item are RESOLVE-decided and get records. Responders, actors, severity setters and action owners are `ref of person`, an undeclared base kind of which the document reader makes no record.

needs.why: Per incident, severity (latest set_at), affected services and the four milestone times are each held as typed claim fields.

needs.need: Who responded to each incident and in what role (incident commander, communications, responder).
needs.declared_by: role_assignment: person (ref person), role (closed)
needs.why: The role is held but the person points at the base kind `person`, of which no record exists, so the reference is dropped (statement_refs.rs:137-142).

needs.need: The timeline of each incident: what was observed or done, when, by whom.
needs.declared_by: timeline_entry: at, entry_kind, actor (ref person), service
needs.why: What and when are held; `by whom` is a ref to `person`, which gets no record, so it is dropped.

needs.need: The root cause stated in the postmortem.
needs.declared_by: root_cause (claim, subject incident, grades postmortem/investigation/hypothesis): cause_kind, contribution, service
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86

needs.need: The follow-up actions from each postmortem, with an owner, a due date and whether each is done.
needs.declared_by: action_item.owner (ref person, by=latest), action_item.due (by=latest), action_item.status (by=latest); follow_up/action_progress claims carry no fields
needs.why: No change.document is declared on a plaintext extractor, so the fold clock is empty (resolution_derived.rs:283-300) and every `latest` fold returns Unordered even on one reading (resolution_derived.rs:685); owner is also a ref to unrecorded `person`.

needs.need: Incidents that are the same outage reported twice are one incident.
needs.declared_by: incident identity_criterion (same outage, however reported)
needs.executed_by: validator: `identity: incident -> RESOLVE under its identity_criterion`
needs.why: RESOLVE decides incident sameness under the criterion.

needs.need: How severity changed during an incident.
needs.declared_by: severity_call: severity, set_at, reason
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86
needs.why: Every severity call is held with its time, so the sequence lists (set_by is dropped, but who set it is not asked).

use_cases.record_types_note: member is metadata-sourced from the author field; project, milestone and task are RESOLVE-decided. The requester is `ref of person` (no record), and member records are offered to a reference only on a document whose own author field names them (pick.rs:1-11), so a member named in another's message is no candidate.

needs.need: Every task we agreed to do, with its owner and due date.
needs.declared_by: task.owner (ref member, by=latest), task.due (time, by=latest)
needs.why: Due runs, but an owner reading lands only on a member the message's own author field names (read_fields.rs:120-149; member is no statement subject, so window_particulars.rs:49-51 drops its mentions), so an owner named by someone else is dropped.

needs.need: Each task's status (open, in progress, blocked, done, dropped) and when it last changed.
needs.declared_by: task.status derived = fold task_status (protocol over status_update)
needs.executed_by: validator: `derived: task.status <- fold task_status by protocol`; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived.rs:148 (derived value written on the record), resolution_derived/protocol.rs:31 (protocol fold over the record's claims); the fold's readings with their report dates are written on the record (resolution_derived/outcome.rs:22-62)
needs.why: The protocol fold sets status and the record row carries its dated history.

needs.need: Which tasks block which other tasks.
needs.declared_by: dependency (claim, subject task): blocked_by (ref task), blocking (blocks/no_longer_blocks)
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed_check.rs:372 (`<claim>.subject` link), typed_match.rs:78-86; ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/statement_refs.rs:137-142 (a statement's ref holds the record its reading names)
needs.why: Blocked tasks reach their blocker by a resolved task reference; the blocker's own status says whether the block still stands.

needs.need: Who asked for each task and why.
needs.declared_by: request (directive claim): requester (ref person), reason
needs.why: Reason is held; requester points at undeclared `person` (is_a follows `specializes` only, type_index.rs:76-81, so member records do not count), and the reference is dropped.

needs.need: Tasks that were reassigned, and to whom.
needs.declared_by: reassignment: from_owner, to_owner (ref member), reason
needs.why: The new owner is usually named by someone else in the message, and a member the document's author field does not name is no Pick candidate (pick.rs:1-11), so to_owner is dropped.

needs.need: Which tasks belong to which project or milestone.
needs.declared_by: task.project (ref project, by=latest), task.milestone (ref milestone, by=latest)
needs.executed_by: ingest/crates/corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/resolution_derived/read_fields.rs:51 (a `by` subject field folds onto the record), read_fields.rs:370
needs.why: project and milestone are RESOLVE-decided, so the references land on records.

use_cases.record_types_note: part is RESOLVE-decided and gets records. Validator: `makes no record of warehouse (entity), technician (entity), supplier (entity): no statement kind is about them, RESOLVE decides none of them and no source supplies them.`

needs.need: Every part, with its part number, description and unit of measure.
needs.declared_by: part.part_number (identity key, no `by`), part.description (by=most), part.unit_of_measure (by=most)
needs.why: Description and unit fold onto the record; part_number is declared without `by`, so it stays on each statement (read_fields.rs:41-54) and RESOLVE writes no identity value onto the record (resolution_records.rs:719-737).

needs.need: How many of each part each warehouse holds, as of the last stock-take and as of the latest movement.
needs.declared_by: stock_count: counted, counted_on, warehouse (ref, unrecorded); movement claims' quantity
needs.why: The balance after the last count is the count plus or minus every later movement, a sum no fold or query computes (typed.rs:134-145); the per-warehouse split also fails because the warehouse reference is dropped.

needs.need: Every movement: a receipt from a supplier, a transfer between warehouses, an issue to a technician, with quantity and date.
needs.declared_by: receipt/transfer/issue: quantity, date, warehouse/from_warehouse/to_warehouse/technician/supplier (refs)
needs.why: Quantity and date are held, but every from/to is a ref to a type with no record (validator warning), so it is removed from the statement (statement_refs.rs:137-142).

needs.declared_by: tension between stock_count only (same subject, warehouse, counted_on); stock_count.expected
needs.why: What the movements imply is a running sum; the tension compares counts with counts, and no filter compares counted with expected (typed_check.rs:216-275).

needs.need: Which technician holds which issued parts.
needs.declared_by: issue.technician, return.technician (ref technician)
needs.why: technician gets no record, so the reference is dropped; holdings would also need issued minus returned.

needs.need: Parts below their reorder level.
needs.declared_by: stock_count.reorder_level, stock_count.counted
needs.why: Both numbers are held on a count, but a filter compares an attribute only with a literal (typed_match.rs:309-345), never with another attribute or a running balance.

gap_tags.ref-target-unrecorded: A reference whose target the document reader makes no record of: an undeclared base kind such as `person`, a declared type with no identity_criterion that no statement is about, or a sourced type named in the text but not in that document's own fields. The reading is never minted into a record and is removed from the statement (resolution_derived/read_fields.rs:93-165, statement_refs.rs:137-142, pick.rs:1-11 'nothing is minted here', document_read/window_particulars.rs:49-51); validate warns only for declared types (document_read/schema.rs:186-216), never for `of = "person"`.
gap_tags.as-of-state: Which records were in a state at a date (today or past) when later statements replace earlier ones or a term runs on past its written end: change.supersedes is read only by the tension comparability pass (corpus-engine/src/enrichment/atlas/analysis/tension_fields.rs:93-102), and a date filter matches every statement, superseded or not (typed_match.rs:309-345). Refuted where the ask is per named record (03 n2 runs by argmax with an lt bound) or the lifecycle is monotone (12 n1 runs by a negated relation); confirmed for a set selected by its current term (02 n5).
gap_tags.computed-value: A value derived by arithmetic from other values (notice date = end date - notice period; agency fee = fee_percent x base salary): the fold registry is first/agree/most/all/earliest/latest/protocol (shared/crates/understanding-vocab/src/ontology/derived.rs:143-158) and paths only walk the graph; nothing computes.
gap_tags.totals: A sum of a quantity over records, per group and period (ordered per supplier, expenses per employee, stock balance from movements, who owes whom): the answer shapes are none/count/argmax/argmin/tally, and tally counts records per value (ingest/crates/understanding-atlas/src/atlas_traversal/typed.rs:134-145, 432-466); no fold sums (derived.rs:143-158).
gap_tags.value-compare: A filter comparing one value with another value (an invoice's amount with its order's total; a count with its reorder level) rather than with a literal: check_filter reads the operand from the query's literal only (typed_check.rs:216-275) and filter_holds compares the attribute with it (typed_match.rs:309-345); a declared tension that does compare is not a relation the typed query can reach (typed_check.rs:278-330).
gap_tags.linked-count-filter: Keeping the records with fewer (or more) than N linked records (requests above 10,000 with fewer than two approvals): argmax/argmin over a related type returns only the extreme (typed.rs:469-533, typed_query_grammar.md:14-18), filters apply to the target's own attributes, and a protocol rule cannot require N distinct moves.
gap_tags.subject-field-unheld: A RESOLVE-decided record's own field (a clause's policy, a part's number) declared without `by`: it stays on each statement and never reaches the record (read_fields.rs:41-54 folds only attributes with `by`; RESOLVE writes no field, resolution_records.rs:719-737), and validate says nothing; the record needs to hold its identity keys and read fields without a fold declaration.
gap_tags.fold-needs-document-date: A `latest`/`earliest` or protocol fold over material whose extractor gives no document date: the fold clock is built only from change.document.date (resolution_derived.rs:283-300), so `latest` returns Unordered even on a single reading (resolution_derived.rs:685) and protocol moves stay pending; no fold can order by a statement's own time field. Shown by a failing need only in 05; the 03 and 12 authors gave up folds for it (03 transcript lines 113-123, 12 transcript assumption 1) but their needs still run by other routes.
